note: No source prints a point for the Treasury of the Acanthians: Wikidata Q22810172 has no coordinate, ToposText has it only as an entity without a location, Pleiades and the Megalithic Portal have no entry, and the SCS paper calls it a 'now-lost treasury'. OpenStreetMap tags a foundation 'Θησαυρός Ακάνθου' (way 145690065, centre about 38.48276, 22.50160, some 45 m from the stored point), but no readable page prints that point, so no two independent quotable points exist.

Port Way is a 58 km linear Roman road from Silchester to Old Sarum; the stored point lies near its Silchester end in Pamber Forest, Wikidata puts a single point near East Anton 42 km away, and Vici.org gives segment points at Overton (51.282761, -1.293303) and Picket Piece (51.23399, -1.441704); no two independent sources give one and the same point for the road, so the point is held for the owner.

Gramalote lies on the Pampa Gramalote in Huanchaco district near Trujillo; the stored point is at Puerto Malabrigo in the Chicama valley, about 50 km away, so it looks wrong. The University of Trujillo's Huanchaco guide gives -8.1000011, -79.1081239, but the other sources with a point (Wikimapia, OSM via Mapcarta) cannot be read as a quotable pair, so no two independent sources can be quoted and the point is held for the owner.

The stored point copies English Wikipedia's 57.4447, 14.1020, which is 57°44′47″N 14°10′20″E misread as decimals and lies some 34 km south of Jönköping; Wikidata and German Wikipedia give the barrow's true place at about 57.7463, 14.1723 in the Ljungarum industrial area, but they are one source family and no independent page (Fornsök/FornPunkt show no WGS84 point, the Megalithic Portal prints a mistyped latitude 53.746389N) could be quoted, so the point is held for the owner.

The ancient site named after the hill is the Stapeley Hill (ring) cairn on the hill's saddle; only the Megalithic Portal prints its point (52.584803N 3.015846W, about 0.2 km from the stored point). The other pages give the hill's summit point or cannot be read (The Modern Antiquarian refuses automated requests), so no second independent source for the site's own point can be quoted.
the new point lies in [], the site says Bulgaria

The stored point is the town of Dolores (and its 'Parque Regional Municipal Ixtutz'), whereas Wikipedia, citing the Atlas Arqueológico, puts the site 8 km south-west of Dolores in the Poxte valley; the Wikidata/Wikipedia point 16.2856, -89.282 lies about 27 km south-east of Dolores and matches no description, and the only quotable point that fits, GeoNames' 16.47296, -89.47832 (copied by Mapcarta), has no independent second source, so the point is held for the owner.

The stored point is Puno city itself, while Wikipedia and MINCETUR place the chullpa site 15-18 km south-west of Puno on the Puno-Moquegua road; only Wikidata (and pages copying it) prints a point (-15.9874, -70.0165), MINCETUR's matching point is not in its visible text, so no two independent quotable sources exist and the point is held for the owner.

The stored point (36.7587, 66.8989) is the city of Balkh, not the site; the only printed points are Wikipedia's coarse 37°5'N 66°43'E and an OpenStreetMap feature (Kutlug Tepe, BALL-666) at 37.08656, 66.69534 shown by Mapcarta in a non-quotable layout, ~1.9 km apart, so no two independent quotable sources agree on the site's point.

The stored point lies about 16 km south-west of El Zotz, but Wikipedia places Bejucal 7 km north-east of El Zotz and 20 km west of Tikal. The only point that fits that description is the OpenStreetMap archaeological-site node 'Bejucal' at 17.2920360, -89.7699608 (openstreetmap.org/node/1699449525). The Wikipedia/Wikidata point (17.42, -89.67) and Spanish Wikipedia's (17.225, -89.616, i.e. Tikal) are both wrong, and no second independent source gives the site's point, so the replacement is held for the owner.

The stored point is the centre of Winsford village (Wikipedia and Wikidata give 51.0993, -3.5652 for the civil parish), not a barrow. Winsford parish holds several scheduled barrows about 1.5-3 km west and south-west of the village (listed on Wikipedia's West Somerset scheduled monuments lists): the Wambarrows round barrow cemetery on Winsford Hill (51.0970, -3.6063), a round barrow 720 m NNW of Spire Cross (51.0966, -3.5917) and four round barrows on The Allotment (51.0882, -3.5822). The entry does not say which of these it is, so no source can be quoted for its point and it is held for the owner.

The site is La Blanca in San Marcos (the Middle Preclassic centre near Ocós); English Wikipedia/Wikidata put it at 14.5951524, -92.1386684, within 0.05 km of the stored point, but no second, independent page prints a point for the site (GeoNames and the Megalithic Portal have no entry, the Authentic Maya page is gone, and aggregators copy Wikidata or give a Petén point), so the point is held for the owner.

No page prints coordinates for La Muerta: Wikidata has no P625, the English, Spanish, French and Italian articles and Commons carry none, GeoNames and the Megalithic Portal have no entry, and the excavation report (Suyuc et al. 2005) only places it 3.5 km south of El Mirador's Tigre complex near the El Mirador-El Tintal causeway; the stored point lies about 5 km south-east of El Tigre, off that line, and an OpenStreetMap GPS node labelled La Muerta sits at 17.73587, -89.91268, but without two quotable sources the point is held for the owner.

Only OpenStreetMap's node 'Column of Taharqa' (25.7187615, 32.6572987) prints the column's point; the Wikidata item was created from that node on 2024-03-16 and copies its coordinates (25.71876, 32.6573), so the two are one source, and no other readable source gives the column's own point.

The entry is the whole class of Hadrian's Wall milecastles - 80 small forts spaced a Roman mile apart along the 117 km Wall - not one site, so no source gives a single point for it; the stored point is a placeholder shared with another entry at Birdoswald fort. Held for the owner.

English Wikipedia places Wajxaklajun at 15°49′43.43″N 91°28′26.23″W beside San Mateo Ixtatán, about 57 km north of the stored point (which lies at Huehuetenango city), and OpenStreetMap via Mapcarta agrees (15.82897, -91.47391), but Mapcarta prints latitude and longitude in a mixed form no quote can hold, and no second independent source family with a quotable point was found; the point is held for the owner, with ~15.8287, -91.4740 as the likely correction.

No source prints a point for the Trypillia settlement itself: the reserve page and the Wikipedia-derived pages only say it lies near Uman, and the stored point (48.6966, 30.1358) is the centre of the village of Kocherzhyntsi, which is not the site.

The site is the Roman villa in Horestone meadow east of Nether Heyford (Northamptonshire HER 829/1). Only Vici.org prints decimal coordinates for it (52.222031,-1.02545, about 0.7 km from the stored point); the HER, RCHME and the Wikipedia list give OS grid references only, and the Wikipedia/Wikidata coordinates are the village's, so no second independent source can be quoted for the villa's point.

All sources place the cave in Allar village on the left bank of the Vilesh (Yardymli district); Russian and Azerbaijani Wikipedia and Wikidata give 38°47′53″N 48°14′13″E, which is the village's own point (GeoNames: Allar 38.799611, 48.232433), about 13.5 km south of the stored point, while the stored point copies English Wikipedia (38.92056, 48.22083), repeated only by Grotto Map citing that article. No independent source gives the cave's own point, so it is held for the owner; the Allar village area (c. 38.80, 48.23) is the likely location.

The stored point near Guatemala City is about 305 km from the site, which lies on the Guatemalan bank of the Usumacinta just downstream of Piedras Negras (Petén); but the only two quotable independent points disagree by about 2 km - Wikidata gives 17°11'0.29"N, 91°16'43.64"W and GeoNames (GNS entry 'Sitio Arqueológico El Porvenir') gives 17.18139, -91.29723 - and no third source settles which marks the site, so the point is held for the owner (either candidate is far better than the stored one).

No two independent pages print a coordinate pair for Chichén Viejo (the Initial Series Group) as visible text. INAH's element page carries 20.670787, -88.572203 only in its map script, which is c. 65 m from the stored point, and the group is described as lying c. 800 m to 1 km south of Las Monjas. The stored point is therefore plausible, but it cannot be sourced by quote.

Only the Megalithic Portal prints a point for the site (Pematang Bango Stone Grave, alternative name Talang Kecepol: 4.025986S 103.205897E, GPS accuracy), 0.23 km south of the stored point, which is a dropped map pin; no second independent source gives coordinates, so the point is held for the owner (suggested -4.025986, 103.205897).

The site is the scheduled round cairn 200 m west of the Margery Hill trig pillar (National Trust HER grid reference SK 1872 9562, about 53.4570, -1.7195), some 0.2 km from the stored summit point; but only the hill's Wikipedia/Wikidata family prints coordinates, and Geograph's photos of the cairn give them only in degrees and decimal minutes, so no two independent quotable sources exist and the point is held for the owner.

The site is the Iron Age cemetery Miłobądz, site 3 (NID register 310/Archeol. of 1976). The stored point and the Wikidata and Wikipedia coordinates are those of the village. The only point given for the cemetery itself is the zabytek.pl map marker (54.132133, 18.720648, about 0.48 km south of the stored point), and it is not in the page's visible text, so no two sources can be quoted for the site's point.

The site is the Celtic ring wall (keltische Fliehburg) on the Ahrenberg just south of the Teufelsrutsch rock; OpenStreetMap places it at 49.7460995, 7.9806731, about 0.3 km from the stored point, but no second independent source prints the fort's own position (Wikipedia's coordinates are those of the rock), so the point is held.
